::: {.why}
Testing an engine against real data can only tell you it produces a number; testing it against a case with a closed-form answer tells you the number is right.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Construct at least two synthetic cases with analytically known strategy returns and assert the engine reproduces them.
- Say what each case tests that the other does not.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Build three cases in tests/: a constant-drift series where a fully invested strategy's return is exact, a deterministic sawtooth where a perfect mean-reversion rule's gross return is exact, and a case with a known cost so the net return is exact. Assert each to tight tolerance.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Make the cost case sharp: with a known turnover and a fixed cost per trade, the annual cost is arithmetic, so assert the engine's reported cost against the hand computation. This catches double-counting of the spread, which is the most common cost bug and one that flatters the strategy.
:::
:::

::: {.deliverable}
Three synthetic test cases with analytic answers, all passing to a stated tolerance.
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
Which of your synthetic tests would catch a spread charged twice, and how tight is the tolerance you set?
:::
